newsitem.title: USA: Spartan Motors sees solid Q4 results.
newsitem.headline: Spartan Motors sees solid Q4 results.

text.p: Spartan Motors Inc said Wednesday it was on track for solid fourth quarter and full-year results.
John Sztykiel, Spartan Motors president and chief operating officer, said in a statement that the company's confidence was based on a strong performance by its transit bus and school bus businesses.
The company also said it hired a chief financial officer.
Earlier, Spartan reported third-quarter net income of $1.2 million, or $0.10 a share, on net revenues of $41.3 million for the third quarter of 1996.
In the same period of 1995, Spartan earned $640,170, or $0.05 a share, on net revenues of $36 million.
Spartan, which makes custom chassis for buses, trucks, motor homes and specialty vehicles, also said its board of directors named Richard Shalter to the post of chief financial officer.

Shalter served for eight years as treasurer and director of finance and administration for Great Lakes Hybrids, a Michigan-based distribution subsidiary of KWS Kleinwanzlebener Saatzucht AG, a German horticultural company.

In the third quarter, Spartan said it sold 742 vehicle chassis compared with 621 a year earlier. In addition, sales at Spartan's bus and specialty chassis unit rose 180 percent through the first nine months of 1996 versus the same period last year.

Sztykiel said the quarter also brought further operating efficiencies. Spartan's third-quarter net profit margin improved to 2.9 percent -- its highest since the first quarter of 1995 and up from 1.8 percent in the same period last year.
The company said it maintained its third-quarter gross margin at 14.8 percent, consistent with the first half of 1996.
